page.layout: One page of text. Heading "ENCOMIASTICON." at the top, centred. Below it a verse poem with a decorated initial C, set in full width. Under the poem, a centred *** ornament, then the catchword "Mox" at the right. Three notes (a), (b), (c) in smaller type at the foot. No margins with text.

main_text.l: Cœlesti ô utinam sit mens afflata
furore, Et possim Magno concaluisse Deo!

l.i: In muri speciem lympha marina stetit;
Munit iter, Jadae tuto transfire potestas

main_text.l: Concaluisse Deo, qui certo tempore Gnatum

l.i: Misit ut orcino nos Pharaone levet.

main_text.l: Concaluisse Deo, qui solvens ora Prophetis

l.i: Hoc populum Vates praemonuisse dedit: Ut
Ut canerem Vatum praesagia; quique revelant,

main_text.l: Quos inter lucet TILLIUS arte cata.

l.i: llius hinc volitat fama per ora virum.

main_text.l: Scilicet apparet doctus simul atque disertus:

page.notes: Decorative woodcut initial C joined to "œlesti". Line "ô utinam" and the "ô" after SALUTIFERI are doubtful, possibly "ô" or "O". "Pharío" is doubtful. "datere" is doubtful, possibly "dare". "Jadae" is doubtful, possibly "Iadae" (read as Jadae). "infescatus" is doubtful. Italic/roman distinctions in the verse are approximate. The *** ornament between the text and the catchword is not transcribed. No page number, running head or signature is printed. Verse is given as one paragraph; the line breaks are not kept.
